name: Stanley Hull
life: “I still remember using my paid hour to cover a colleague's daughter's birthday.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, where Stanley notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I am the foreman who cannot offer both options. I have put my own paid hour into the pot.
appearance: Stanley is easy to recognize by auburn hair cut square at the nape and a crooked front tooth visible when laughing. Usually dressed in a cropped bottle-green coat with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead, Stanley draws small circles on a tabletop while waiting when listening.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Stanley takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To offer an hour that lets both retirees choose.
family: Tess Walker is Stanley’s half-sibling. Stanley asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Tess remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The Saturday swap*, Tess says, “I want to swap so I can meet the sister my father only mentioned in his will.”
connections: Clyde Schmidt. The foreman's hour gives the younger hand a real chance to work beside the departing crew.

reactions.situation: The two old workers are offered separate farewell days
reactions.response: Stanley asks each worker separately what kind of last day they want.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Stanley asks them privately what can be shared about the delay and respects the answer.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Stanley asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
